_comment: The contract between the harnesses and the score.
Every dimension that contributes to the rating is listed here, with the
harness responsible for it. `tool/rate.dart` REFUSES to print a score if a
listed dimension never reported — because the alternative is what this repo
did before: a harness that did not run and a harness that found nothing
printed the identical result, and 'no findings' was indistinguishable from
'no measurement'. That is the whole reason the number moved between runs.
That paragraph was AN ASPIRATION, NOT A FACT, until an adversarial audit
reproduced the hole: with all seven harness paths pointing at nonexistent
files the tool printed 100/100, 5.00/5, 'manifest OK' and exit 0. It could
not have worked, either — a clean dimension emitted no output at all, so
'clean' and 'never ran' were the same bytes. Each harness now emits one
`DIM|<id>` beacon per dimension it measures, via `reportMeasured()` in
test/support/perf_rating.dart, and rate.dart requires one per entry below.
If you add a dimension here, its harness MUST beacon it or every run is
INVALID. That is the intended failure direction.
The `sev` field below is now what PRICES a finding. A harness that emits a
different severity for its own dimension makes the run INVALID rather than
silently repricing its own defect.
Severity is priced in test/support/perf_rating.dart: P0 -40, P1 -15, P2 -5.
4.5/5 == score 90 == zero P0, zero P1, at most two P2, across the whole app.
The first twelve dimensions all measure STRUCTURE: does it build, does it
overflow, is the text visible, are the targets big enough. Every one of them
can be green on a screen a blind user cannot operate, that ignores the
reduce-motion preference, that offers a new user nothing to do, and that
answers a finished session with silence. The app scored 95/100 while
`Semantics(` appeared zero times in the whole Focus feature.
That is not the score being wrong, it is the score being blind. The four
dimensions after `alignment-drift` add EXPERIENCE, held to the same standard
as the rest: each is a count or a boolean against a citable standard or a
structural contract in this codebase. Taste stays out of the number, and
docs/rating.md is explicit that delight is not something this tool can see.

dimensions.source: binary: the screen threw while building
binary: a perpetual animation costs battery unobserved
binary: the screen threw while building
RenderFlex overflow at a supported width/text scale
binary: a screen with no text is not a screen
header chrome must be one line at every supported size

WCAG ratio from Color.computeLuminance against the nearest opaque ancestor; gradient subtrees skipped; gated only under 1.5:1 because the measured failure was 1.05:1 and no legitimate pairing lands there
geometry assertion on the laid-out render tree (shared left edges, square ring, centred clock, equal grid cards)

WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (Level A) — count of nodes in the real semantics tree carrying a tap/longPress action with no label, value, tooltip or hint; the property Flutter's own labeledTapTargetGuideline asserts

WCAG 2.2 SC 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions — binary: SchedulerBinding.transientCallbackCount still above zero after 6s idle with disableAnimations true. Paired with an opposite assertion that the motion still runs when allowed, so the gate cannot be cleared by deleting the animation
structural: a fresh install must render an EmptyState with a non-null action. Requiring the shared widget is the load-bearing half — a hand-rolled empty Column carries no action contract to check
structural: ToastOverlay.hasActiveToasts after driving a real session to completion with the screen mounted. Defaults to a finding, so an unmeasured run cannot read as a clean one

excluded.why: ProcessInfo.currentRss inside flutter test is dominated by the harness itself and differs every run. Adding it would reintroduce exactly the non-determinism this file exists to remove. Its deterministic proxy is disposal-leak, which is not yet wired.

Measured on device by integration_test/z01_perf_e2e_test.dart and REPORTED, never scored. An emulator's GPU is the host's, and the build-cost harness observed an ~8x wall-clock swing between two runs of an identical screen. Every scored dimension here is a count, a boolean, or a within-run ratio, on purpose.
meetsGuideline(textContrastGuideline) over-reports on this app's gradient theme. Needs a scoped run before it can be trusted enough to price.
